manifest.task: Place the avocado, onion, tomato, and bell pepper on the cutting board.
manifest.brain: GPT proxy (Codex session), not trained RynnBrain
manifest.executor: analytical OSC controller with simulator-state localization

brain.Cause: The gripper closed too high above the counter and no ingredient visibly followed the lift; avocado pickup failed.
brain.Sub: Lower the contact height and grasp the avocado again.
brain.Fine: Realign from above, close at the side of the object, and lift vertically to verify a secure grasp.

brain.Cause: The avocado remains near the counter edge after another empty lift; the grasp orientation did not secure it.
brain.Sub: Change gripper orientation and grasp the target again.
brain.Fine: Rotate 90 degrees above the target, descend onto the other pair of sides, close, and lift to verify.

brain.Cause: After changing orientation, the avocado has left the counter and follows the gripper.
brain.Sub: Place the avocado on one side of the board, leaving room for the other ingredients.
brain.Fine: Maintain the grasp, align the object center over the board, descend and release, then withdraw to inspect the landing point.

brain.Cause: The avocado remains on the board after withdrawal; the other three ingredients are still outside it.
brain.Sub: Grasp the tomato next instead of stopping after one target.
brain.Fine: Align over the rear tomato, close and lift, then place it in free board space after verifying attachment.

brain.Cause: The tomato remains on the rear counter; the vertical approach did not pick it up.
brain.Sub: Change wrist orientation and approach the tomato again.
brain.Fine: Adjust the gripper above the tomato, slightly raise the side contact point, close, and verify after lifting.

brain.Cause: The tomato still has not lifted; repeated rear grasps failed, so a different approach angle is needed.
brain.Sub: Tilt the gripper and approach from the front of the counter.
brain.Fine: Open the gripper, descend with a tilted wrist to either side of the tomato, and verify reachability before closing.

brain.Cause: The tilted approach has placed the fingers beside the tomato, closer to the intended contact than before.
brain.Sub: Close on the tomato at the current position.
brain.Fine: Keep the wrist angle, close slowly, then retreat and lift with the same orientation to check the result.

brain.Cause: The gripper has closed, but the arm occludes the object; lifting is still needed to verify attachment.
brain.Sub: Retreat from the rear space and lift the tomato.
brain.Fine: Maintain the tilt and closure, retreat toward the front and rise, then check whether the tomato follows.

brain.Cause: The lift and retreat are complete; partial occlusion means attachment still needs verification after placement.
brain.Sub: Move the grasped contents to the other side of the board and inspect the landing point.
brain.Fine: Keep the grasp while approaching free board space, release low, withdraw, and check whether the tomato stays on the board.

brain.Cause: The tomato landed on the counter to the right of the board; the post-transport landing point still needs correction.
brain.Sub: Grasp the tomato again at its new position.
brain.Fine: Approach from the more open front area, grasp and lift, then move it to free board space.

brain.Cause: After grasping from the front, the tomato follows the gripper; pickup has recovered.
brain.Sub: Place the tomato in free board space.
brain.Fine: Align its center with the rear-right free area, descend, release, and withdraw to check whether it is inside the board.

brain.Cause: The avocado is on the board, but the tomato remains to its right and the other ingredients are not all in place; the full task is incomplete.
brain.Sub: End this continuous attempt and retain partial recovery and the incomplete outcome.
brain.Fine: Save the current view and official task outcome; a successful grasp does not establish success on the four-ingredient task.
